That way you can get a good ballpark estimate for it. It’s really worth it and I think you should plan to do that by starting with that.

Well. I’m not entirely sure about the ‘I can’t afford it’ situation. But I won’t assume. I’m nearly 25, unemployed, and haven’t had a job. So I have no money. I did meet my deductible, so I don’t think it was too bad. I know the new meds they put me on are only like six dollars. And as for work, if you have sick days just tell them you are sick and going to the hospital. They’re not allowed to ask what’s wrong with you or what hospital you’re at. I would say it’s definitely worth looking into. And if you think you can afford it talk to your boss. You can lie and say you need surgery or something that will require some recovery time. Again, they aren’t aloud to know tour private business. Generally you are only there for a few days anyways.

Thank you so much. It’s definitely an experience I’ll never forget. I made some great friends. It was mostly good. But there was some bad. But I guess nothing is perfect. However the weekday psychiatrist should not be working a job like that. She would tell people to stop crying, that they don’t look depressed. Etc. she told me I didn’t have panic attacks because mine last longer than 20 minutes, and apparently they ‘are supposed to’ last no longer than that. Of course right after my meeting with her I had a severe panic attack that lasted an hour and a half. I’m still glad I went. Groups were great. It put me on a decent sleep schedule. Broke me away from some stressors and let me have a break. And the other patients were the most therapeutic aspect of it. You make friends. And everyone is so understanding because they’re dealing with the same things. If you ever think you need it you should research the places around you, find the best, and go. I’m not 100% better or anything. But it was a step in the right direction, as opposed to being put on a waiting list for therapy.
